text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. Given the location on the nape of the neck and the lack of pain or fever, this presentation is highly suggestive of a lipoma or a cyst rather than a metastatic lesion or infection. I have ordered an ultrasound to confirm the nature of the mass and rule out any deeper structural involvement.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Well-circumscribed lesion in the subcutaneous tissue suggestive of a cystic nature.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound results indicate a well-circumscribed cystic lesion, which aligns with your symptoms of a painless, progressive swelling on the nape of the neck. Given the location and characteristics, this is most consistent with an epidermoid cyst. DIAGNOSIS READY: Epidermoid cyst of the neck
